Here\'s a summary of the diagnosis and fix.\n\n## Diagnosis\n\nThe Info page (`InfoActivity` → `content_info.xml`) renders a single `TextView` bound to `@string/large_text`:\n\n```xml\n<TextView ... android:text="@string/large_text" />\n```\n\nIn `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`, that string contained only the GPL preamble. It stopped mid-way through the terms:\n\n```\n"TERMS AND CONDITIONS\\n"\n"0. Definitions:"\n"\\"This License\\" refers to version 3 of the GNU General Public License.\\n"\n"..."\n```\n\nSo scrolling to the bottom of the Info page showed a literal `...` placeholder instead of the rest of the license — exactly the "License is not completely written down" report. Sections 1–17, `END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS`, and the application notice were all absent.\n\n## Fix\n\nReplaced `large_text` with the **complete GPL v3 text taken from the repository\'s own `LICENSE` file** (the authoritative copy already shipped in the project, so the displayed license can\'t drift from the actual one), keeping the existing `License - GPL V 3.0` heading.\n\nMechanically, the value is now one XML line where:\n- `<` / `>` / `&` are XML-escaped (`&lt;`, `&gt;`, `&amp;`) — needed for the FSF/GNU URLs like `<https://fsf.org/>`\n- inner double quotes are escaped as `\\"` and apostrophes as `\\\'` (e.g. `"This License"`, `developers\' and authors\'`)\n- line breaks are `\\n` escapes\n- the whole value is wrapped in real double quotes so aapt preserves the license\'s indentation and double-space runs rather than collapsing them\n\n## Verification\n\n- `./gradlew clean assembleDebug` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**\n- Inspected the compiled `resources.arsc` in the output APK to confirm aapt didn\'t mangle the resource:\n  - all of `0. Definitions`, `16. Limitation of Liability`, `17. Interpretation of Section`, `END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS`, `why-not-lgpl` are present\n  - the old `...` placeholder is gone\n  - escapes resolved properly: `"This License"` renders with real quotes, `\\n` became real newlines, and the whitespace-preserving outer quotes were stripped rather than shown literally\n\nOnly `strings.xml` changed; no layout or Java code was touched, so no other functionality is affected.\n\nOne process note worth flagging: my first attempt silently produced the wrong output because I passed the replacement text directly to Python\'s `re.sub()`, which interprets backslash escapes in the replacement string and turned every literal `\\n` back into a raw newline. I caught it when the file line count came out at 718 instead of ~43, and fixed it by using a lambda replacement.
